# @primer/react-tailwind 0.0.0

> Primer design system components implemented with Tailwind CSS and Base UI. This file is generated; do not edit it by hand.

Guidance for coding agents and LLMs generating code that uses this package.

`@primer/react-tailwind` implements the Primer design system with Tailwind CSS and Base UI. It is a separate implementation from `@primer/react`, not a compatibility layer. Guidance written for `@primer/react` is frequently wrong here.

## Setup

Render the app inside `ThemeProvider` and `BaseStyles`, and import the stylesheet once at the entry point.

```tsx
import '@primer/react-tailwind/styles.css'
import {BaseStyles, ThemeProvider} from '@primer/react-tailwind'
;<ThemeProvider colorMode="auto">
  <BaseStyles>{app}</BaseStyles>
</ThemeProvider>
```

Import components from the root or from a component subpath. Both resolve to the same implementation.

```tsx
import {Button} from '@primer/react-tailwind'
import {Button} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Button'
```

## Rules

- Style with `className`. There is no `sx` prop and no styled-system props such as `m`, `p`, `bg`, or `color`. Reaching for `sx` is the most common mistake when adapting `@primer/react` code.
- Use Primer semantic Tailwind utilities such as `text-default`, `bg-muted`, and `border-default` rather than raw palette values such as `text-gray-500`. Colors must resolve through Primer tokens so themes and high-contrast schemes keep working. A build check rejects hardcoded colors.
- Not every default Tailwind utility exists. The Primer type scale replaces the default one, so `text-base` and `text-lg` generate nothing; use `text-body-medium`, `text-body-large`, or a title size. There are no `ring-*` or `bg-border-*` color utilities either. When no utility exists, use the token directly, as in `bg-[var(--borderColor-muted)]`.
- Focus treatment is `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-focus`.
- Change the rendered element with `render` on Base UI-backed components such as `Button`, `Dialog`, and `Tooltip`, and with `as` on presentational components such as `Text`, `Stack`, `Card`, and `PageLayout`. Check the component's props before choosing.
- React 19 is the only supported peer. The package is compiled with React Compiler; do not add manual `memo`, `useMemo`, or `useCallback` wrappers around package components for performance alone.
- Components forward their root ref and unrecognized DOM props to their root element. Prefer passing standard DOM props directly instead of wrapping components in extra elements.
- There is no `Box` component. Use a plain element with `className`, or `Stack` for layout.

## Composition

Compound components expose Base UI-style parts, commonly `Root`, `Trigger`, `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Popup` or `Content`, `Title`, `Description`, and `Close`. Use the documented parts rather than recreating behavior with generic elements, because the parts carry the focus, dismissal, and ARIA wiring.

```tsx
<Dialog>
  <Dialog.Trigger render={<Button>Open</Button>} />
  <Dialog.Content>
    <Dialog.Title>Title</Dialog.Title>
  </Dialog.Content>
</Dialog>
```

Do not nest interactive elements. To make a component navigate, pass an anchor through `render` instead of placing an `<a>` inside a button.

## Choosing a component

- Action in the current view: `Button`. Navigation: `Link`, or `LinkButton` for button styling. Icon-only: `IconButton` with a required `aria-label`.
- Choosing from a known list: `ActionMenu` for commands, `SelectPanel` for a filterable picker, `Select` for a short native list, `Autocomplete` for free text with suggestions.
- Status and metadata: `Label` for general metadata, `StateLabel` for issue and pull request state, `CounterLabel` for counts.
- Messaging: `Banner` for page-level status, `Dialog` when the message must block the task, `FormControl` validation for a single field.
- Announcing asynchronous changes: `Announce`, or `AriaStatus` and `AriaAlert` for a fixed politeness. There is no component named `LiveRegion`.

## Names that changed from `@primer/react`

Experimental and versioned components are promoted to their stable names. Use `Dialog`, not `DialogV2`. Use `Tooltip`, not `TooltipV2`. Use `SelectPanel`, not `SelectPanel2`. Use `Breadcrumbs`, not `Breadcrumb`.

Deprecated APIs are not included. Use `NavList` instead of `SideNav`, `TextInput` with `Token` composition instead of `TextInputWithTokens`, and Octicons with your own styling instead of `CircleBadge`.

## Accessibility

Every interactive control needs an accessible name. `IconButton` requires `aria-label`. Associate form controls with `FormControl`, or with a native label, rather than placing text beside an input. Announce asynchronous updates with `Announce` or `AriaStatus` instead of moving focus.

## Verifying generated code

If a prop is uncertain, read the shipped TypeScript declarations rather than assuming the `@primer/react` signature. Each component directory also ships `README.mdx` for usage and `ALIGNMENT.md` for differences from the legacy component.

## Components

### ActionBar

Import: `import {ActionBar} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ActionBar'`

`ActionBar` groups related actions with `Button`, `IconButton`, `Group`, `Divider`, and `Menu` parts.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace `overflowIcon` with an explicit `ActionBar.Menu`; preserve the action order and focus behavior in consumer code.

### ActionList

Import: `import {ActionList} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ActionList'`

`ActionList` is a semantic action, menu, or listbox list composed from explicit child parts.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use `loading` with `loadingText` for an unavailable item that is waiting on work. Loading items expose disabled semantics, render a shared spinner, and suppress trailing actions until ready.

### ActionMenu

Import: `import {ActionMenu} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ActionMenu'`

`ActionMenu` is a composable Base UI menu with button and low-level trigger options.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Compose branded triggers with `render`, not `as`, to avoid nested interactive elements. Use `className` when the composed control owns the visual treatment.

### AnchoredOverlay

Import: `import {AnchoredOverlay} from '@primer/react-tailwind/AnchoredOverlay'`

`AnchoredOverlay` positions a dismissible overlay relative to a trigger.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace legacy `outside-*` placement names with `side` and `align`.

### Autocomplete

Import: `import {Autocomplete} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Autocomplete'`

`Autocomplete` is a composable Base UI autocomplete for filtering and choosing from a known set of options.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Move legacy token, dialog, and TextInput integrations to composition with their local components.

### Avatar

Import: `import {Avatar} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Avatar'`

`Avatar` renders a user or organization image at a consistent size and shape. Use `square` for organizations and other non-person entities.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace responsive size objects with responsive `className` utilities on the Avatar or its layout wrapper.

### AvatarStack

Import: `import {AvatarStack} from '@primer/react-tailwind/AvatarStack'`

`AvatarStack` is a presentational component for a compact, expandable group of avatars. Import it from `@primer/react-tailwind/AvatarStack`.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace the import path with `@primer/react-tailwind/AvatarStack`.

### Banner

Import: `import {Banner} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Banner'`

`Banner` announces a page-level status or message that needs attention but does not interrupt the user. Use `Dialog` instead when the message must block the task, and inline validation for a single field.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Prefer the compound parts for custom heading and action markup.

### Blankslate

Import: `import {Blankslate} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Blankslate'`

`Blankslate` provides a structured empty state with optional visual, heading, description, and primary or secondary actions.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing composition and variant props can be retained.

### BranchName

Import: `import {BranchName} from '@primer/react-tailwind/BranchName'`

`BranchName` renders a Git ref name in Primer's monospace branch treatment. It is presentational; pass `href` to make it navigable.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Compose Tooltip, live announcements, and selection controls around BranchName instead of expecting BranchName props for them.

### Breadcrumbs

Import: `import {Breadcrumbs} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Breadcrumbs'`

`Breadcrumbs` communicates the current location within a hierarchy.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Normal breadcrumb and item composition is intended to be drop-in.

### Button

Import: `import {Button} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Button'`

`Button` triggers an action in the current view. Use `LinkButton` when the control navigates to a URL, and `IconButton` when the control has no visible label.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Prefer LinkButton for navigation; the `link` Button variant remains available for semantic button actions rendered as inline links.

### ButtonBase

Import: `import {ButtonBase} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ButtonBase'`

`ButtonBase` is the unstyled button primitive behind `Button`, `IconButton`, and `LinkButton`. Reach for it only when building a new button-like control; prefer `Button` for ordinary actions.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- The component is a stable replacement for the experimental legacy export.

### ButtonGroup

Import: `import {ButtonGroup} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ButtonGroup'`

`ButtonGroup` joins related buttons into a single segmented control. Use `SegmentedControl` instead when the buttons select between mutually exclusive views.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Compose a local Tooltip or ActionMenu around grouped controls rather than passing overlay behavior to ButtonGroup.

### Card

Import: `import {Card} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Card'`

`Card` is a composable content container with heading, description, image, metadata, icon, and action parts.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Compose ActionMenu or native action controls inside `Card.Action` instead of relying on a Card-specific menu API.

### Checkbox

Import: `import {Checkbox} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Checkbox'`

`Checkbox` is a form-associated binary control. Pair it with a native label or `FormControl.Label`.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep a native label or FormControl label associated with each checkbox.

### CheckboxGroup

Import: `import {CheckboxGroup} from '@primer/react-tailwind/CheckboxGroup'`

`CheckboxGroup` groups checkbox primitives and supplies their shared controlled or uncontrolled state.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use `Label`, `Caption`, and `Validation` parts for group metadata; set `visuallyHidden` only when another visible label exists.

### ConfirmationDialog

Import: `import {ConfirmationDialog} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ConfirmationDialog'`

`ConfirmationDialog` asks a user to confirm or cancel a consequential action.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Migrate `onClose` gesture handling to `onCancel`/`onConfirm` and controlled Root state.

### CounterLabel

Import: `import {CounterLabel} from '@primer/react-tailwind/CounterLabel'`

`CounterLabel` displays a numeric count alongside a label, such as an open-issue total. It is presentational and does not format or abbreviate the number.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep `variant`, children, and count-related content unchanged.

### DataTable

Import: `import {DataTable} from '@primer/react-tailwind/DataTable'`

`DataTable` is a presentational, typed table for stable row data. It owns native table structure, sorting state, and column layout while `Table` exposes structural parts for custom composition.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- **Intentional:** Fetching, error dialogs, and product action menus are not configuration props on the base table. Compose `Table.Skeleton`, `Table.Pagination`, `ActionMenu`, and error UI in the application instead.

### Details

Import: `import {Details} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Details'`

`Details` is a native disclosure element with a styled summary.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Remove `useDetails`; use the native `open` attribute/event behavior or normal React state around Details when needed.

### Dialog

Import: `import {Dialog} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Dialog'`

`Dialog` provides a modal surface with composable trigger and content parts.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Migrate custom structure to the Tailwind compound parts.

### FeatureFlags

Import: `import {FeatureFlags} from '@primer/react-tailwind/FeatureFlags'`

`FeatureFlags` scopes boolean flags and `useFeatureFlag` reads one flag.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Provider and hook usage is intended to be drop-in.

### FilteredActionList

Import: `import {FilteredActionList} from '@primer/react-tailwind/FilteredActionList'`

`FilteredActionList` is a configured, data-driven filterable ActionList for established picker and command-list patterns. It composes shared `TextInput`, ActionList content layers, `Checkbox`, `Spinner`, and `SkeletonBox` with Base UI's combobox behavior. Use `ActionList` directly when consumer-owned markup needs a different structure.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Deprecated `trailingIcon` and `trailingText` are not included; use `trailingVisual`.

### Flash

Import: `import {Flash} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Flash'`

`Flash` presents a prominent message with semantic visual variants and an optional full-width layout.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Put a named close button and its state outside or inside Flash as ordinary composition.

### FormControl

Import: `import {FormControl} from '@primer/react-tailwind/FormControl'`

`FormControl` is a composable field wrapper that provides label, caption, validation, and control association.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Package controls consume FormControl metadata automatically; use `FormControl.Control` for a native input or `useFormControlForwardedProps` when authoring a custom control.

### Header

Import: `import {Header} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Header'`

`Header` is a compact horizontal header primitive. Use `Header.Item` for layout participants and `Header.Link` for consistently styled navigation.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing Header subcomponent composition can generally be retained.

### Heading

Import: `import {Heading} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Heading'`

`Heading` renders a section heading. Choose the level with `as` for document structure and `variant` for visual size, so heading order stays correct independently of scale.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Rename `variant` to `size`.

### Hidden

Import: `import {Hidden} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Hidden'`

`Hidden` conditionally hides presentational content at Primer viewport ranges. It is not a permission or authorization mechanism.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep range decisions in `when`; add visual styling with `className` on the wrapper.

### IconButton

Import: `import {IconButton} from '@primer/react-tailwind/IconButton'`

`IconButton` is a button whose only content is an icon. `aria-label` is required, because the control has no visible text.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Supply an accessible name with `aria-label`; use native `title` only as supplemental text.

### InlineMessage

Import: `import {InlineMessage} from '@primer/react-tailwind/InlineMessage'`

`InlineMessage` communicates validation, status, and availability inline with content or a form control.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing variant and content usage can be retained.

### IssueLabel

Import: `import {IssueLabel} from '@primer/react-tailwind/IssueLabel'`

`IssueLabel` displays a colored label and can render as a link, button, or custom element for interactive label workflows.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Import the stable Tailwind `IssueLabel` instead of the experimental legacy entry point.

### KeybindingHint

Import: `import {KeybindingHint} from '@primer/react-tailwind/KeybindingHint'`

`KeybindingHint` renders a compact, screen-reader-friendly keyboard shortcut using the local key formatting rules.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Pass the documented key tokens through `keys`; do not depend on a story platform override.

### Label

Import: `import {Label} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Label'`

`Label` marks an item with a short piece of metadata, such as a status or category. It is presentational and does not label form fields; use `FormControl.Label` for that.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing `variant`, `size`, and semantic `as` usage can be retained.

### LabelGroup

Import: `import {LabelGroup} from '@primer/react-tailwind/LabelGroup'`

`LabelGroup` lays out a collection of `Label` items and collapses overflow behind a toggle when they exceed the available width.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- `visibleChildCount="auto"` uses `ResizeObserver` rather than the legacy `IntersectionObserver`. This produces deterministic counts on resize and avoids relying on clipping intersection behavior.

### Link

Import: `import {Link} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Link'`

`Link` navigates to another location. Use `Button` when the control performs an action, and `LinkButton` when a navigation target needs button styling.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Preserve `muted`, `inline`, and `as` usage.

### LinkButton

Import: `import {LinkButton} from '@primer/react-tailwind/LinkButton'`

`LinkButton` navigates to a URL while looking like a `Button`. It renders an anchor, so it requires `href` rather than `onClick`.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace `as={RouterLink}` with `render={<RouterLink to="/path" />}`.

### LiveRegion

Import: `import {LiveRegion} from '@primer/react-tailwind/LiveRegion'`

`LiveRegion` announces asynchronous changes without moving focus.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Select `AriaStatus` for polite status updates and `AriaAlert` for urgent messages; do not duplicate the text in multiple regions.

### NavList

Import: `import {NavList} from '@primer/react-tailwind/NavList'`

`NavList` is a vertical navigation primitive for settings and page navigation.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use native `href` anchors; router adapters and reload-button APIs are unsupported.

### Overlay

Import: `import {Overlay} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Overlay'`

`Overlay` is a low-level surface for positioned content.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Do not treat Tailwind `Overlay` as a drop-in modal/menu controller.

### PageHeader

Import: `import {PageHeader} from '@primer/react-tailwind/PageHeader'`

`PageHeader` composes page context, a title, description, actions, and local navigation while preserving reading and focus order.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Compose Breadcrumbs, local Header, and product controls around the slots instead of extending PageHeader.

### PageLayout

Import: `import {PageLayout} from '@primer/react-tailwind/PageLayout'`

`PageLayout` composes page headers, navigation panes or sidebars, content, and footers into a responsive layout.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep bottom sheets and filter/menu controls in application composition.

### Pagination

Import: `import {Pagination} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Pagination'`

`Pagination` renders previous, next, and page links from a controlled current page and page count.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- `onPageChange(event, page)` keeps upstream's event-first signature rather than the package's usual `(value, details)` order, so existing handlers port unchanged.

### Popover

Import: `import {Popover} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Popover'`

`Popover` pairs a trigger with positioned, dismissible content.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Recompose legacy anchor/content markup with the compound parts.

### Portal

Import: `import {Portal} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Portal'`

`Portal` renders children outside their React parent's DOM subtree while preserving React context.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace `containerName` with a DOM `container` or ref.

### ProgressBar

Import: `import {ProgressBar} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ProgressBar'`

`ProgressBar` displays determinate progress as a single segment or as a composed set of `ProgressBar.Item` segments.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Rename `barSize` to `size` and `bg` to `variant`. The middle size is `medium` rather than upstream's `default`, matching the size vocabulary used across the package.

### Radio

Import: `import {Radio} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Radio'`

`Radio` is a styled radio primitive for use in a `RadioGroup`.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use a visible label or associated FormControl label for every radio.

### RadioGroup

Import: `import {RadioGroup} from '@primer/react-tailwind/RadioGroup'`

`RadioGroup` is a Base UI radio group with roving focus and single-value selection.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange` for group selection; do not duplicate the primitive's state.

### RelativeTime

Import: `import {RelativeTime} from '@primer/react-tailwind/RelativeTime'`

`RelativeTime` renders a semantic `time` element with a human-readable relative value and a stable machine-readable date.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- `date` and `datetime` are normalized onto the `time` element's machine-readable `datetime` value.

### ScrollableRegion

Import: `import {ScrollableRegion} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ScrollableRegion'`

`ScrollableRegion` owns horizontal or vertical overflow and becomes a labelled, focusable region when its content overflows.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing children, native scrolling props, accessible-name props, and scroll usage can generally be retained.

### SegmentedControl

Import: `import {SegmentedControl} from '@primer/react-tailwind/SegmentedControl'`

`SegmentedControl` is a single-choice Base UI toggle group for related view or mode choices.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange` for single-choice state.

### Select

Import: `import {Select} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Select'`

`Select` is a styled native `<select>` with Primer control tokens. Native browser behavior owns option menus, keyboard operation, focus, form association, and controlled or uncontrolled values.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace `Select.Trigger`, `Value`, `Portal`, `Positioner`, `Popup`, `List`, `Item`, `Group`, and `GroupLabel` with `Select`, native options, and optgroups.

### SelectPanel

Import: `import {SelectPanel} from '@primer/react-tailwind/SelectPanel'`

`SelectPanel` is a data-driven, filterable picker built with Base UI Combobox and Primer's Popover and Dialog primitives.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- `onOpenChange(open, gesture)` reports the gesture that caused the change rather than Base UI change details, and `disableFullscreenOnNarrow` stays opt-out where `FilteredActionList` uses the opt-in `fullScreenOnNarrow`. Both keep upstream's contract.

### SkeletonAvatar

Import: `import {SkeletonAvatar} from '@primer/react-tailwind/SkeletonAvatar'`

`SkeletonAvatar` reserves circular or square space for an avatar while the profile content is loading.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing `size` and `square` usage can be retained.

### SkeletonBox

Import: `import {SkeletonBox} from '@primer/react-tailwind/SkeletonBox'`

`SkeletonBox` reserves space for content that is loading, using a shimmer placeholder that can be delayed until a request has taken long enough to show.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep Suspense, data fetching, and loading transitions in the application.

### SkeletonText

Import: `import {SkeletonText} from '@primer/react-tailwind/SkeletonText'`

`SkeletonText` creates one or more text-shaped loading lines with typography height presets and an optional maximum width.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Expect at least one line; fractional counts are floored.

### Spinner

Import: `import {Spinner} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Spinner'`

`Spinner` communicates that work is in progress with an animated indicator and an optional screen-reader announcement.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep `size`, `srText`, and delay usage, but recheck selectors targeting the legacy SVG root.

### SplitPageLayout

Import: `import {SplitPageLayout} from '@primer/react-tailwind/SplitPageLayout'`

`SplitPageLayout` is an opinionated full-width `PageLayout` composition for settings and detail pages with a navigation pane and content area.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use the local PageLayout-compatible slot and responsive props rather than legacy styling wrappers.

### Stack

Import: `import {Stack} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Stack'`

`Stack` arranges related content along one axis with token-based spacing, alignment, wrapping, and responsive direction.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Do not assume omitted `gap` means zero; it keeps the normal spacing default.

### StateLabel

Import: `import {StateLabel} from '@primer/react-tailwind/StateLabel'`

`StateLabel` shows the lifecycle state of an issue or pull request, such as open, closed, or merged. Use `Label` for general-purpose metadata.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep the accessible text explicit rather than depending on color alone.

### SubNav

Import: `import {SubNav} from '@primer/react-tailwind/SubNav'`

`SubNav` is a horizontal secondary navigation bar composed from `SubNav.Links` and `SubNav.Link`.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing navigation composition and state ownership can be retained.

### Tabs

Import: `import {Tabs} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Tabs'`

`Tabs` provides unstyled tab, tab list, and tab panel behavior that can be composed into an application-specific presentation.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use `value`, `defaultValue`, and `onValueChange` for selection state.

### Text

Import: `import {Text} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Text'`

`Text` applies Primer typography to inline or block text. Use `Heading` for section headings so that structure is conveyed semantically.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Preserve core typography props and semantic `as` usage.

### Textarea

Import: `import {Textarea} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Textarea'`

`Textarea` is a styled native multiline text control.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace `block` and pixel-height props with `className` sizing utilities or native rows/cols.

### TextInput

Import: `import {TextInput} from '@primer/react-tailwind/TextInput'`

`TextInput` is a styled native single-line input with small, medium, and large visual sizes.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Continue using `leadingVisual`, `trailingVisual`, `trailingAction`, `loading`, and `characterLimit`.

### Timeline

Import: `import {Timeline} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Timeline'`

`Timeline` is a presentational compound activity stream built from `Item`, `Badge`, `Body`, `Actions`, `Avatar`, and `Break` parts.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Compose local Avatar, StateLabel, links, and actions inside Timeline parts.

### ToggleSwitch

Import: `import {ToggleSwitch} from '@primer/react-tailwind/ToggleSwitch'`

`ToggleSwitch` is a form-associated binary switch with small and medium sizes.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use the checked-state contract; do not mirror Base UI state in a second React state source.

### Token

Import: `import {Token} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Token'`

`Token` displays compact filter or selection content with optional leading visuals, selection state, and removal behavior. `IssueLabelToken` provides the same token interaction model with a custom label color.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Do not nest a remove button inside a link/button token.

### Tooltip

Import: `import {Tooltip} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Tooltip'`

`Tooltip` provides supplementary text for a trigger.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Replace `direction` with physical `side` and use `align` where needed.

### TopicTag

Import: `import {TopicTag} from '@primer/react-tailwind/TopicTag'`

`TopicTag` presents a repository topic as a compact accent-colored tag. `TopicTagGroup` wraps tags into a responsive row.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing TopicTag and TopicTagGroup composition can generally be retained.

### TreeView

Import: `import {TreeView} from '@primer/react-tailwind/TreeView'`

`TreeView` is a presentational compound component for hierarchical files, folders, and nested resources. Compose its parts in author order to retain control of item content and visuals while TreeView owns tree semantics, expansion, roving focus, and typeahead.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Control expansion with `expanded`, `defaultExpanded`, and `onExpandedChange` where needed.

### Truncate

Import: `import {Truncate} from '@primer/react-tailwind/Truncate'`

`Truncate` applies single-line overflow truncation while preserving the full value in the native `title` tooltip.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Keep expansion state and controls in the consumer.

### UnderlineNav

Import: `import {UnderlineNav} from '@primer/react-tailwind/UnderlineNav'`

`UnderlineNav` is a presentational navigation composition for sibling destinations. It keeps native link semantics, while consumers own route integration, item order, and selected state.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- **Intentional — composition:** Wrap items in `UnderlineNav.List`. This preserves native `nav`/`ul`/`li`/link semantics without extracting or reordering consumer children.

### UnderlinePanels

Import: `import {UnderlinePanels} from '@primer/react-tailwind/UnderlinePanels'`

`UnderlinePanels` is a tab-and-panel composition with an underlined tab list.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Use the documented value/default-value callback contract for tab selection.

### VisuallyHidden

Import: `import {VisuallyHidden} from '@primer/react-tailwind/VisuallyHidden'`

`VisuallyHidden` hides content visually while keeping it available to screen readers. Use it for context that is obvious visually but missing from the accessible name.

Differences from `@primer/react`:
- Existing `focusable` usage can be retained.

## Not included

- `CircleBadge` (deprecated). Use an Octicon from @primer/octicons-react with your own styling.
- `SideNav` (deprecated). Use NavList.
- `TextInputWithTokens` (deprecated). Compose TextInput with Token.
- `Breadcrumb` (deprecated). Use Breadcrumbs.
- `SelectPanel2` (deprecated). Use SelectPanel, which is the promoted implementation.
- `useRefObjectAsForwardedRef` (deprecated). Pass ref as a prop; React 19 supports ref forwarding without a hook.
- `useResponsiveValue` (deprecated). Use responsive class names or CSS media queries.
